changes_vs_current: Biggest reshuffle: Tetris (avg 35.75, #33; VGC #1, RS #2 but GI reader vote #115 and not in Edge top 20), Minecraft (37.75), Super Mario Bros (58.7), Pokemon Red/Blue (48.3), Pac-Man (135.7), Street Fighter II (43.3), Portal 2 (36.8), CoD4 (33.5), GoldenEye (52), Melee (52.3), Mario Kart 8 (104), Fortnite (87.3) all fall out; new entrants are RE4, Mass Effect 2, RDR1, Super Metroid, MGS, Super Mario World, Shadow of the Colossus, WoW, A Link to the Past, BioShock, Chrono Trigger, Dark Souls. Elden Ring only holds #24 on two sources (Edge #9, RS #44) because VGC and GI 2018 predate it.
confidence: low-medium. All four sources skew toward critics and hardcore console/PC gamers, and Edge is truncated to its top 20, which punishes mass-market titles (Tetris, Minecraft, Super Mario Bros, Pokemon, Pac-Man, Fortnite) under the 'length+5' rule. If you want a party-game audience, consider keeping Tetris and Minecraft (Tetris is VGC #1 and RS #2; Minecraft is Edge #13). Corroboration not in the math: Game Informer's 2024 reader bracket (200k+ votes) crowned Ocarina of Time over Skyrim, with The Last of Us and RDR2 in the final four (gameinformer.com/GameGauntlet2024, fetched). IGN's 2024 Top 100 could not be fetched (404, Wayback offline) and British GQ 2023 (239 experts) yielded only its top 3 (BotW, TLOU, Tetris) via videogamecanon.com, so neither was used. VGC overlaps with the other lists, so sources are not fully independent. Top 3 (BotW, OoT, TLOU) is solid; the rest are close, with a 1.5-point spread across positions 19-24.
